model.name: Localization / Language
model.purpose: Provide an embeddable, format-neutral declaration of locale, translation and terminology binding, so that any adopting entity can state which language, script and locale conventions apply to it, express and resolve linguistic preferences, and reference translated resources and convention profiles without duplicating them.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-031 is a mixin that attaches linguistic and locale context to a host record. It covers BCP 47 language-tag identity and canonical form; the binding of subtags to the IANA Language Subtag Registry including deprecation and replacement; Unicode locale identity with -u and -t extension fields; script identity and base-direction/writing-mode hints; ordered preference declarations, available-locale inventory and the explicit resolved-locale outcome with fallback reasons; the role distinction between content language, intended audience and user-interface locale; versioned references to translated resources, terminology assets and formatting/collation convention profiles; and the governance needed to keep every declaration reproducible against a pinned data version. It declares context; it does not hold localized content, run translation production, identify people or places, or execute access, retention or audit decisions.
in_scope: BCP 47 language-tag identity, well-formedness, validity and canonical form, covering language, extlang, script, region, variant, extension and private-use subtags
Binding to the IANA Language Subtag Registry, including Deprecated and Preferred-Value handling, grandfathered and redundant registrations, Scope classification and macrolanguage caveats
Unicode locale identity as distinct from language identity, including -u and -t extension fields, their canonicalization and likely-subtag expansion
Script identity by ISO 15924, Suppress-Script handling, declared base direction and character/line order hints carried together with the value they qualify
Ordered or weighted preference declarations, basic and extended language ranges, available-locale inventory and the configured default locale
Matching, filtering and lookup outcomes recorded as requested, available and resolved locale with an explicit fallback chain and per-step reason
Role distinction between content language, intended audience and user-interface locale, and between declared, detected and negotiated values
Versioned references to translated resources, terminology assets and number, date, time, unit and collation convention profiles
Governance of the mixin itself: pinned registry and CLDR data versions, canonicalization policy, provenance fields and reproducibility records
out_of_scope: The localized content itself: translated text, media, their versions and editorial state
Translation production workflow, vendor assignment, translation memory operation and terminology approval processes
Person, party or account identity; a language preference is bound to a party by the party model, not defined here
Geographic territories, boundaries, political status and legal jurisdiction; a region subtag is neither a location nor a legal fact
Calendar, numbering, collation, measurement and time-zone rule data; only selection keys and pinned references are held
Character encoding, Unicode normalization, text segmentation, font selection, shaping and the bidirectional algorithm itself
Machine-translation and language-detection engines; only their identity, output and confidence are recorded
Execution of access decisions, erasure requests, retention schedules and audit-trail storage
Currency amounts, pricing and monetary conversion, even where a currency key appears in a locale extension

boundary_notes.neighbor: Localized content and resource models (documents, strings, media assets)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model declares which language, script and locale apply to a value or resource; the resource model owns the text, its versions, its editorial state and its publication lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party, person and account profile models
boundary_notes.distinction: A stated language preference is an attribute the party model binds to a party. This model defines the shape and provenance of the preference declaration only, and never treats a preference as an identity attribute or capability assertion.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Geographic region, territory and jurisdiction models
boundary_notes.distinction: A region subtag identifies a locale variant. Territory geometry, political status, nationality and legal jurisdiction belong to those models and must never be inferred from a language or locale tag.

boundary_notes.neighbor: CLDR convention data and its implementations (calendars, collations, numbering, measurement, time zones)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records the selection keys and the pinned data version. The convention definitions and the formatting, sorting and parsing behaviour remain in the referenced data and the implementing library.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Translation production and terminology management systems
boundary_notes.distinction: This model binds a resource to a locale and can record the source language of transformed content. Job state, vendor assignment, review gates and terminology approval are owned by those systems.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Access control, privacy and audit models of the adopting Dimension
boundary_notes.distinction: This model classifies preference data as potentially linkable and supplies reproducibility fields. Policy evaluation, enforcement, erasure execution and audit-trail retention are owned and executed there.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Text rendering and bidirectional layout engines
boundary_notes.distinction: This model supplies the paragraph direction and orientation hints as metadata. The Unicode bidirectional algorithm, shaping, line breaking and glyph selection are performed by the rendering engine.

sources.title: RFC 5646: Tags for Identifying Languages
sources.relevance: Normative syntax and semantics of language tags: the langtag ABNF, subtag types, case conventions, canonical form, well-formed versus valid, grandfathered and redundant registrations, and the Language Subtag Registry record format including Deprecated, Preferred-Value, Prefix, Suppress-Script, Macrolanguage and Scope.

sources.title: RFC 4647: Matching of Language Tags
sources.relevance: Normative definition of basic and extended language ranges, language priority lists, basic filtering, extended filtering and lookup with progressive truncation, the requirement to define defaulting behaviour when no tag matches, and the statement that matching does not require validating tag semantics.

sources.title: IANA Language Subtag Registry
sources.relevance: The authoritative record set for subtag validity, carrying Type, Subtag/Tag, Description, Added, Deprecated, Preferred-Value, Prefix, Suppress-Script, Macrolanguage, Scope and Comments; the File-Date supplies the version pin used for reproducible validation.

sources.title: UTS #35: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML), Part 1: Core
sources.relevance: Defines the Unicode language identifier and Unicode locale identifier, canonical syntax and LocaleId canonicalization with alias replacement, the -u extension key inventory (ca, co, nu, hc, fw, ms, rg, sd, tz, va and others), the -t extension, likely-subtag addition and removal, and CLDR language matching.

sources.title: UTS #35: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML), Part 2: General
sources.relevance: Layout elements characterOrder and lineOrder, the constraint linking horizontal and vertical values, and the statement that layout data supplies the paragraph direction without overriding bidirectional ordering; also locale display-name elements and the display-name algorithm.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Accept-Language as a weighted language priority list, Content-Language as the language of the intended audience rather than a single-language restriction, the caveat that a stated preference may not describe a user's actual capability, and the fingerprinting and privacy risk of language preference signals.

sources.title: RFC 6067: BCP 47 Extension U (Unicode Locale)
sources.relevance: Registers the 'u' singleton, names the Unicode Consortium and CLDR as maintaining authority, defines attribute and keyword syntax, and states that only the first occurrence of a duplicated attribute or key conveys meaning and that canonical form is lowercase and ordered.

sources.title: RFC 6497: BCP 47 Extension T - Transformed Content
sources.relevance: Registers the 't' singleton for content produced by transliteration, transcription or translation; defines the tlang source language tag and tfield mechanism subtags, requires the source tag to be a canonical regular language tag, and forbids irregular tags and duplicate field separators.

sources.title: ECMA-402: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification
sources.relevance: Operational definitions of CanonicalizeUnicodeLocaleId and CanonicalizeLocaleList, the requested / available / resolved locale triad, LookupMatchingLocaleByPrefix and best-fit matching, the localeMatcher option, DefaultLocale, and the reporting of resolved Unicode extension values via resolvedOptions.

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: The lang, xml:lang and dir attributes
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of the language of a node, the meaning of an empty lang value as unknown language, the dir attribute values ltr, rtl and auto, the pragma-set default language derived from Content-Language metadata, and the precedence of an element-level declaration over document-level metadata.

sources.title: Strings on the Web: Language and Direction Metadata
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) Internationalization Working Group
sources.version_or_date: W3C First Public Working Draft, 16 July 2026
sources.relevance: Best practice that language and base direction be carried as metadata at string or document level rather than inferred, the value/lang/dir carrier pattern, first-strong detection as a last-resort fallback, the requirement to isolate inserted strings, and the recommendation against embedding direction control characters in values.

sources.title: Choosing a Language Tag (W3C Internationalization Questions)
sources.version_or_date: W3C i18n guidance article, no revision date published; accessed 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: Non-normative implementation guidance on keeping tags as short as the distinction requires, honouring Suppress-Script, preferring individual language subtags over macrolanguages for new work while retaining legacy macrolanguage tags, and avoiding private-use subtags because they defeat interoperability.

sources.title: ISO 15924 Code Lists
sources.organization: Unicode Consortium, acting as ISO 15924 Registration Authority
sources.relevance: Authoritative four-letter script codes with English and French names and Unicode property value aliases, plus the exceptionally reserved codes Zyyy-adjacent entries such as True and Root; consulted and found to expose no normative script direction property.

bundles.name: Linguistic and locale identity
bundles.description: Everything needed to state, normalize and validate which language, script and locale a host record is bound to, and to keep that binding stable as external registries change.
bundles.rationale: BCP 47 separates a tag's syntax from its validity against a registry, and UTS #35 separates a language identifier from a locale identifier. An agent cannot safely compare, store or display a linguistic declaration without all three of these settled first: the canonical tag, its registry backing, and the script and direction it implies.

bundles.name: Preference, availability and locale resolution
bundles.description: How a linguistic preference is declared, what is actually available to satisfy it, and how the two are reconciled into a single resolved locale with a recorded, reproducible reason.
bundles.rationale: The matching standard defines ranges, filtering and lookup but explicitly leaves the no-match default to the application, and the internationalization API separates requested, available and resolved locales while permitting an implementation-defined best-fit matcher. An agent therefore cannot infer the outcome from the inputs and must be told the inventory, the scheme and the recorded fallback reason.

data_elements.description: The confidence reported by the detector for a detected value.

data_elements.name: Assertion event time
data_elements.description: The event time at which the declaration was asserted, recorded separately from the time this model ingested it.

data_elements.name: Scope precedence rank
data_elements.description: The rank used to decide which of several overlapping declarations governs a given value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role, asserting party and the declared-versus-detected pair are qualifying attributes of the host record's locale annotation. They have no independent existence and must be read together with the value they qualify, so an artifact would fragment the declaration.

functions.name: Parse and canonicalize a language or locale identifier
functions.description: Parses a supplied identifier into its subtags by role, applies the stated case and ordering normalization, and returns the canonical form together with the parse result and the list of normalizations applied.
inputs: Canonicalization profile selector: language-tag canonical form or Unicode locale identifier canonical form
Pinned registry and locale data versions to use
outputs: Parsed subtag structure by role, including extension attributes and keywords
Well-formedness verdict with the failing position where parsing fails
List of normalizations applied, including dropped duplicate attributes and keys
preconditions: The input is a single identifier, not a language range or a priority list
The canonicalization profile and its data version are stated explicitly by the caller
effects: Produces a canonical identifier and a parse result for storage or comparison
Records which normalization profile and data version were applied so the result is reproducible
Performs no content transformation, no rendering and no resource selection

functions.name: Validate subtags against the pinned subtag registry
functions.description: Checks every subtag of a well-formed identifier against a pinned subtag registry snapshot and reports validity, deprecation, the prescribed replacement, and the prefix and script-suppression advisories attached to the matching records.
inputs: Well-formed identifier or a parsed subtag structure
Pinned registry snapshot reference including its File-Date
Policy for handling deprecated, grandfathered and collection-scope records
outputs: Deprecation status and prescribed replacement value per affected subtag
References to the individual registry records consulted
Prefix and script-suppression advisories, and scope classification of the primary language subtag
preconditions: The identifier has already passed well-formedness parsing
A registry snapshot is pinned, retrievable and integrity-checked
effects: Emits a validation result bound to a named registry snapshot and File-Date
Flags grandfathered, redundant, collection-scope and macrolanguage records for human review
Does not rewrite the stored identifier; applying a replacement is a separate, policy-governed patch

functions.name: Filter or look up tags against language ranges
functions.description: Applies basic filtering, extended filtering or lookup to compare a language priority list against a set of candidate tags, returning either the matching set in priority order or the single closest match with its truncation steps.
inputs: Language priority list of ranges with optional weights
Defaulting behaviour to use when no candidate matches
outputs: Matching tag set in priority order for filtering schemes
Single closest tag or the declared default for lookup
Match reason per candidate, including the truncation steps taken
List of ranges that matched nothing
preconditions: Ranges and candidate tags are expressed in the same canonical form
The defaulting behaviour for a no-match result is defined before the call is made
effects: Returns a match result without asserting the semantic validity of any tag or range
Records the scheme, implementation and truncation steps used so the result can be reproduced
Selects no resources, serves no content and writes to no host record

functions.name: Resolve declared preferences to a resolved locale
functions.description: Resolves an ordered preference declaration against an available locale inventory and a configured default, producing the resolved locale, the outcome class, an ordered fallback chain with a reason per step, and the extension values actually honoured.
inputs: Ordered preference declaration with its declared-versus-inferred markers
Reference to an available locale inventory manifest and its version
Configured default locale and defaulting behaviour
Matching scheme selector and unknown-extension-key policy
outputs: Outcome class: exact, fallback, default or none
Ordered fallback chain with a reason code per step
Extension key values actually honoured, with substitutions marked
Data versions consulted: inventory version, registry File-Date and locale data release
preconditions: The inventory manifest version and the registry snapshot are both identified in the call
Declared and inferred components of the preference are distinguishable in the input
The caller is authorised to read any party-linked preference supplied
effects: Produces a resolution outcome record for the requesting context
Reports which requested extension values were honoured and which were substituted
Does not enforce access, execute rendering, or write to the referenced audit or retention models

composition.target: IETF BCP 47 language tag and language tag matching standard
composition.purpose: Adopt the normative tag syntax, subtag roles, canonical form, well-formed versus valid distinction and the basic filtering, extended filtering and lookup schemes. Alignment is claimed for the structures actually cited; no conformance claim is made for behaviour this model does not execute.

Dereference every subtag to its registry record for validity, deprecation, Preferred-Value replacement, Prefix, Suppress-Script, Macrolanguage and Scope. This model pins a snapshot by File-Date and carries record references; it does not maintain, extend or republish the registry.

composition.target: Unicode CLDR and UTS #35 locale identity and locale data
composition.purpose: Adopt the Unicode locale identifier, its canonical syntax and alias-based canonicalization, likely-subtag expansion, the -u and -t extension field structures, and the layout orientation elements. Divergence from BCP 47 canonical form is recorded as a conflict rather than silently reconciled.

Bind the script subtag to an authoritative four-letter script code and its record. Script naming and code assignment stay with the registration authority; no direction property is imported because the consulted code list publishes none.

composition.target: Any adopting Dimension entity that carries linguistic context, such as content records, catalogue entries, party preferences and message payloads
composition.purpose: Embed the locale declaration alongside the value it qualifies so that value, language and direction travel together. The host entity keeps its own identity, lifecycle and access class; this mixin adds only the linguistic declaration and its provenance.

composition.target: Party, person and account profile model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Carry the preference declaration and its provenance while the party model owns the binding of that preference to a person or account. A language preference is never treated here as an identity attribute or as evidence of capability.

composition.target: Localized content, document and terminology resource models
composition.purpose: Point from a locale declaration to the translated resource or terminology asset it applies to, by identifier and version. Content storage, versioning, editorial state and translation production remain entirely with those models.

composition.target: Access control, privacy, retention and audit models of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Supply the retention class, linkability classification and reproducibility fields that those models need. Policy evaluation, enforcement, erasure execution and audit-trail storage are owned and performed there; this reference grants this model none of those semantics.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable owner for the Dimension's locale declaration set and for the pinned subtag registry and locale data versions it validates against.

Publish, as versioned configuration, the default locale, the defaulting behaviour when nothing matches, the matching scheme permitted on each negotiation surface, and the policy for applying registry-prescribed replacements.
Declare which host models embed this mixin and which of their fields carry value, language and direction together, so that direction metadata is never separated from the value it qualifies.
Record, for every negotiation surface, whether an implementation-defined best-fit matcher is permitted and which implementation and version is in use.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use the canonical language tag or Unicode locale identifier as the natural key within a loc-locale namespace, and store the as-received form beside it when the two differ. Qualify Dimension-local vocabulary with a private-use subtag or a separately namespaced attribute so it can never collide with a registered subtag or a future extension key. Never reuse a locale identifier as the primary key of a host entity: the same identifier legitimately appears on many unrelated records.
registry_links: IANA Language Subtag Registry snapshot pinned by File-Date, used as the sole validity authority for language, script, region, variant, grandfathered and redundant records.
ISO 15924 script code list maintained by the Unicode Consortium as registration authority, used for script codes and their aliases.
Unicode CLDR BCP 47 extension key and type data referenced by the -u and -t extensions, pinned to a named data release.
Unicode CLDR locale data release supplying likely subtags, layout orientation and language matching data.

canonicalization_rules: Store identifiers in exactly one stated canonical form and record which one: language-tag canonical form or Unicode locale identifier canonical form. The two differ for extended-language and alias replacement and must never be compared across forms without re-canonicalizing first.
Apply the recommended casing - lowercase language, titlecase script, uppercase region - as a presentation convention only; comparison and lookup remain case-insensitive.

Sort variant subtags and extension singletons, order extension attributes and keywords by the Unicode canonical rules, keep only the first occurrence of a duplicated attribute or key, and remove type values that mean true.
Retain the as-received identifier alongside the canonical form whenever they differ, so canonicalization remains auditable by the owning Dimension.
Record the canonicalization profile name and the data release version with every canonical value; a canonical form without its profile is not reproducible.
patch_rules: Changing a canonical identifier is a replacement, not an in-place edit: record the previous value, the reason (registry deprecation, correction or re-declaration), the asserting party and the effective event time.
Applying a registry-prescribed replacement requires naming the registry File-Date that prescribed it; a replacement applied without that pin is rejected.
Adding or removing extension keys patches the locale identifier only; it never implies any change to the referenced convention profiles or to the content the declaration qualifies.
A detected value may be added or updated freely, but must never overwrite a declared value; precedence is resolved at read time by the recorded rule.
Resolution outcome records are immutable; a correction is appended as a new record that references the one it supersedes.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional subtag, extension key or metadata attribute is backward compatible; changing the primary language subtag, the declaration role, or the semantics of a resolved locale is breaking.
Consumers must ignore extension keys they do not recognise rather than reject the identifier, and must report back the values they actually honoured.
Do not claim conformance to a matching scheme whose implementation is host-defined; record best-fit results as implementation-dependent and store the matcher identity and version with them.
Widening a registry pin to a newer snapshot is a compatible change only if no stored identifier becomes invalid or newly deprecated; otherwise it requires a reconciliation decision.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the host record, catalogue entry, interaction or job carrying the locale declaration.
Governed global identifier: the canonical language tag or Unicode locale identifier, resolved against a pinned subtag registry record or a named locale data release identifier.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither a master-system identifier nor a governed global identifier exists.
A registry File-Date, locale data release number, manifest generation time or resolution timestamp is a version pin or ordering key and is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record every time value as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Where they can differ, record the event time - when a preference was stated, a declaration asserted, a replacement made effective or a resolution performed - separately from the observation or ingestion time at which this model received, validated or indexed it. Never collapse the two into a single field, and never derive one from the other.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - registry snapshots, inventory manifests and resolution outcome records - are named by their stable scope identifier plus a monotonic version or a ULID, never by their generation date alone. The registry File-Date, manifest version and locale data release are carried as separate version fields so that a name change and a version change stay distinguishable.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest together with the identity and version of everything it was derived from: registry File-Date, locale data release, matcher implementation and inventory version. A resolution outcome record is invalid, and must not be relied on, if it cannot name the inventory manifest version and the registry snapshot it consulted.

policies: A language, locale, script or region subtag never establishes nationality, ethnicity, jurisdiction, legal residence or physical location. Any such inference is prohibited and must be rejected at validation rather than merely discouraged.

Declared, detected and negotiated values are stored in distinct fields. A detected or inferred value must never overwrite a declared one, and its detector identity and confidence must be retained alongside it.

Convention profiles, translated content, translation processes and terminology assets are bound by identifier and version only; their data is never copied into this model, so that no second unowned source of truth is created.

Language preference data is treated as potentially linkable personal data with a recognised fingerprinting risk. Its retention, disclosure and secondary use follow the adopting Dimension's privacy policy, which owns those decisions; this model records only the classification.
A stated preference is not a capability claim. Absence of a locale from a preference list must never be read as inability to understand it, and presence must never be read as proficiency.

read: Resolve a stored identifier to its parsed subtags, its registry record references and its declared roles, always reporting the registry snapshot the verdict was computed against.
Read the current preference declaration, the inventory version in force and the most recent resolution outcome for a given scope as a consistent set.
Consumers may cache canonical forms but must revalidate against the registry snapshot named in the record before treating a cached validity verdict as current.
Reading a party-linked preference or outcome record requires the host record's access class; reading a registry snapshot or script code list requires none.
create: Create a locale declaration only with a stated role, an asserting party reference and an event timestamp; a declaration with no role is rejected.
Reject creation of an identifier that is not well-formed, and record a validity verdict against a named registry snapshot before the declaration becomes effective.
Creating an inventory manifest or a resolution outcome record requires naming every data version it was derived from.
Creating a detected value requires the detector identity, version and confidence; a detected value may not be created without them.
update: Update a canonical identifier only through an explicit replacement that records the previous value, the reason, the asserting party and the effective event time.
Update deprecation status by revalidating against a newer registry snapshot and recording that snapshot's File-Date; never silently rewrite a stored identifier when the registry moves.
Update the available inventory by issuing a new manifest version rather than editing an existing one, so that earlier outcome records remain reproducible.
Corrections to a resolution outcome are appended as a superseding record; existing outcome records are immutable once written.
delete: A locale declaration is removed only together with the host record it annotates. This model writes a tombstone carrying the identifier, role, asserting party, effective interval and removal reason, and retains no copy of the annotated content.

Preference declarations and resolution outcome records that contain or link to party-identifiable preference data carry a retention class assigned here, but the adopting Dimension's retention schedule and erasure policy own the disposition decision and its execution.

Pinned registry snapshots and inventory manifests are retained for as long as any outcome record or validity verdict cites them; once no citation remains they are disposed of under the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy. Deletion of the externally published registry data itself is controlled by its publisher and is outside this model entirely.

Physical deletion, erasure-request handling, legal-hold suspension and audit-trail preservation are executed by the referenced access, privacy, retention and audit models of the adopting Dimension. This mixin supplies the tombstone and the retention class and never performs or authorises the deletion itself.

roles.name: Locale governance owner
responsibilities: Approves the Dimension default locale, the no-match defaulting behaviour and the policy for applying registry-prescribed replacements.
Owns the pinning cadence and upgrade decisions for the subtag registry snapshot and the locale data release.
Signs off on any divergence recorded between canonicalization profiles.

roles.name: Language data steward
responsibilities: Validates stored declarations against the pinned registry snapshot and reconciles deprecation drift when a newer snapshot is adopted.
Maintains the available locale inventory, its completeness measures and its refresh cadence.
Curates the meaning of any private-use subtags in use and decides whether they may cross an external interface.

roles.name: Host model owner
responsibilities: Embeds the mixin, guarantees that value, language and direction travel together on every carrier, and owns the lifecycle and access class of the annotated record.
Declares the scope precedence order when several declarations apply to the same value.
Initiates removal of declarations when the host record is removed.

roles.name: Internationalization reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews script, direction and writing-mode declarations and challenges values that were produced by a heuristic rather than declared.
Approves the matching scheme for each negotiation surface and any use of an implementation-defined best-fit matcher.
Reviews new variant, extension and macrolanguage usage against current guidance before it is adopted.

roles.name: Privacy and access authority (referenced, not owned here)
responsibilities: Owns the classification, retention schedule and disclosure rules for party-linked preference and outcome data.
Executes erasure decisions, access decisions and audit-trail retention; this model supplies only the declaration, the retention class and the reproducibility fields.

access.default_rule: Locale declarations attached to non-personal content are readable by any consumer entitled to read the host record, because they are display metadata that the value cannot be rendered correctly without. Preference declarations and resolution outcome records linked to an identifiable party are not readable by default and inherit the host record's access class.
exceptions: Preference lists and resolution outcome records tied to an identifiable party require authorization from the host party model, because language preference signals are a recognised fingerprinting and linkability vector.
Pinned registry snapshots and script code lists are public reference material; they carry no read restriction beyond integrity protection and provenance.
Private-use subtags may encode Dimension-internal semantics and are withheld from external interfaces unless the governance owner has explicitly published their meaning.
Aggregate availability manifests may be exposed publicly where they describe published resources, but per-party resolution outcomes may not be derived from them.
audit_requirements: Record which registry snapshot, locale data release and inventory manifest version each resolution consulted, so the outcome can be recomputed.
Record the asserting party and the event time for every declaration, every replacement and every override, separately from the ingestion time.
Record the matcher identity and version whenever an implementation-defined scheme was used, because the result is not otherwise reproducible.

Storage, retention and inspection of audit trails are performed by the adopting Dimension's audit model; this model supplies the reproducibility fields and asserts no audit-trail semantics of its own.

required_fields: Pinned subtag registry snapshot and its File-Date
Default locale and the defaulting behaviour when no requested range matches
Canonicalization profile in force and the permitted matching schemes
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before performing any read or write, whatever the storage or interface projection in use.

Read the pinned registry snapshot reference and the locale data release version, then the identity bundle - tag identity, registry binding, script and direction - before interpreting, comparing or displaying any identifier.
Read the preference, availability and resolution layer before performing or trusting any negotiation result, and never assume a default locale that the configuration has not declared.
Read the adopting Dimension's privacy, retention, access and audit policy references before creating, reading or removing any party-linked preference or resolution outcome record.

coverage.claim: WM-XCT-031 delivers a format-neutral, embeddable declaration of linguistic and locale context: language-tag identity with canonical form and well-formed-versus-valid separation, binding to a pinned subtag registry with deprecation and prescribed replacement, script identity and explicit base-direction and orientation metadata, Unicode locale identity with its extension fields, ordered preference declarations, a versioned available-locale inventory, and an explicit resolved locale with a reasoned fallback chain, plus versioned references to translated resources, terminology assets and convention profiles and the governance that keeps every declaration reproducible. It is grounded in IETF BCP 47, the IANA Language Subtag Registry, Unicode UTS #35 and ISO 15924, ECMA-402, the HTML Living Standard and W3C Internationalization material. It deliberately excludes localized content, translation production, party identity, geography, jurisdiction, rendering, and the execution of access, retention or audit decisions.

checklist.notes: Canonical tag and locale identifier, subtag structure, well-formed versus valid, private-use handling and a three-tier identity priority that puts the master-system identifier first and rules out dates as identifiers.

The lifecycle owned here is that of the declaration and its registry backing: added, deprecated, replaced by a prescribed Preferred-Value, superseded or tombstoned. The lifecycle of the annotated content and of the party is explicitly left to the host models.

Eight composition links distinguish standards alignment, registry reference, mixin embedding and referenced party, content and access models; boundary notes name seven neighbours and the distinction against each.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset, with event time separated from observation or ingestion time for preference capture, assertion, replacement effectiveness and resolution; registry File-Date and data releases are treated as version pins, not identifiers.
Registry snapshot pinning with digest, canonicalization profile and version, matcher identity and version, detector identity and confidence, and asserting party for every declaration.
Five roles including a referenced privacy and access authority; convention behaviour, content and party binding are explicitly assigned to neighbouring models rather than claimed.

Two-stage validation - syntactic well-formedness then registry validity against a named snapshot - with prefix, script-suppression, scope and macrolanguage advisories, plus an integrity rule that invalidates any outcome record that cannot name its data versions.

Default rule separates display metadata on public content from party-linked preference and outcome data, with four scopes, four exceptions and audit reproducibility fields. Evaluation and enforcement are referenced, never owned.

Tombstone for the declaration, retention classes for party-linked records, cite-count-based retention for snapshots and manifests, and an explicit statement that erasure execution, legal hold and audit-trail preservation are performed by the adopting Dimension's referenced models.

Alignment with BCP 47 and UTS #35 is claimed only for cited structures; conflicts between the two canonicalization regimes are recorded rather than resolved, unknown extension keys must be ignored rather than rejected, and honoured values must be reported back.

Script identity, suppression and inference are separated; base direction is required as explicit metadata with first-strong detection recorded as a last-resort fallback, and character and line order come from locale layout data. The absence of a direction property in the script code list is recorded as a conflict.

No consulted source defines an interoperable best-fit matching algorithm. Basic filtering, extended filtering and lookup are deterministic and normatively specified, but best-fit behaviour is implementation-defined, so the model mitigates rather than closes this by requiring the matcher identity and version to be stored with every outcome.

Deliberately excluded. A region subtag identifies a locale variant and is not a place; territory geometry, political status and physical location belong to the geographic and jurisdiction models and a policy forbids inferring them here.

known_omissions: The ISO 639 and ISO 3166-1 code sets were not consulted directly because they are not openly published; they are reached only through the registry records that quote them, so no claim is made about clauses of those standards.

CLDR supplemental script metadata, including per-script right-to-left flags and sample characters, was not retrieved. Direction guidance rests on the layout orientation elements and the HTML direction attribute instead.
CLDR language matching distance data and its weights are referenced but not enumerated, so no matching quality thresholds are specified here.
The full -u and -t key and type vocabularies change with each locale data release and are referenced rather than listed; the keys named in questions are illustrative, not exhaustive.

Sign languages, constructed languages, historical orthographies and transliteration schemes are handled only through registered variant subtags and the transformed-content extension; no consulted source justified additional structure.
Text segmentation, character encoding, Unicode normalization form, font selection and shaping were excluded because no consulted primary source places them inside a locale declaration.
Terminology and glossary assets are bound by reference only; the internal structure of a term base was not researched and is left to the referenced terminology model.
conflicts: BCP 47 permanently reserves the second and third extended-language positions and permits a tag such as an extlang form written after its macrolanguage, while UTS #35 canonicalization replaces the extended-language subtag with its preferred value. The two canonical forms of the same input differ and must never be compared directly.

BCP 47 canonical form replaces subtags that carry a registry Preferred-Value, whereas UTS #35 and ECMA-402 canonicalization additionally apply CLDR alias data. An identifier that is canonical at the transport layer may not be canonical at the application layer.

RFC 4647 defines deterministic basic filtering, extended filtering and lookup, but ECMA-402 permits an implementation-defined best-fit matcher and allows implementations to accept further localeMatcher values with implementation-defined behaviour. Results are therefore not portable between hosts.

RFC 9110 allows Content-Language to name several tags describing the intended audience, while the HTML Living Standard derives a pragma-set default document language from such metadata. A multi-tag value does not yield a usable single document language, so the two uses must be kept distinct.

The ISO 15924 code list consulted assigns script codes but exposes no normative direction property. Base direction must therefore come from locale layout data or an explicit declaration and cannot be derived from the script code alone.

W3C Strings on the Web: Language and Direction Metadata is a First Public Working Draft. Its value, language and direction carrier pattern is cited as best practice and must not be represented as a normative requirement.

The registry snapshot consulted, File-Date 2026-08-08, deprecates collection-scope subtags with a prescribed replacement. Identifiers validated against an earlier snapshot may already be deprecated, which is why every verdict must name its snapshot.
regional_assumptions: Region subtags may be two-letter country codes or three-digit numeric codes; the numeric form is preferable where an alpha assignment is contested or has changed, and neither form asserts a jurisdiction, a nationality or a place of residence.

No default locale is assumed anywhere in the model. Any fallback locale is a configuration decision of the adopting Dimension and must be declared explicitly, including the behaviour when nothing matches at all.
Statutory language obligations such as official-language requirements, mandatory translation and labelling law are jurisdiction-owned facts and are not derivable from any tag in this model.

Right-to-left handling assumes the consuming environment implements the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. This model supplies the paragraph direction and isolation requirement only and performs no reordering itself.
Where a language is written in more than one script across regions, the script subtag is treated as the discriminator and the region subtag is never used as a proxy for it.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether a region subtag could be used to infer jurisdiction, nationality or physical location. Rejected: no consulted source supports the inference, and an explicit policy now requires validation to reject it rather than merely discourage it.

Tested whether a stored Accept-Language preference could serve as a party attribute or a stable identifier. Rejected: RFC 9110 notes that a stated preference may not describe actual capability and that the field is a fingerprinting vector, so it is held as party-linked, access-restricted, non-identifying data.

Tested whether ISO 15924 supplies script direction. No such property was found in the consulted code list, so direction is sourced from locale layout data or explicit metadata and the divergence is recorded as a conflict rather than papered over.

Tested whether the resolution outcome record could be presented as an audit trail or as an enforcement decision. Rejected: it records the outcome of this model's own declaration, while evaluation, enforcement, erasure and audit-trail retention remain with referenced models and are named as such in the deletion and audit rules.

Tested whether convention data - calendars, collations, numbering systems, measurement, time zones - could be modelled locally now that the extension keys are in scope. Rejected: only selector keys and versioned references are retained, because copying the data would create a second unowned source of truth for behaviour this model does not execute.

Tested whether undetermined, multiple-language and no-linguistic-content values could be treated as ordinary tags or as missing data. Rejected: they carry distinct meanings and are handled as explicit exception values with their own precedence rule, never as a null or as a default.

Searched for a normative, interoperable definition of best-fit locale matching and found none; determinism is recorded as a checklist gap and mitigated by storing the matcher identity and version, rather than being asserted.

Tested whether an automatically detected language could be promoted into the declared field once confidence is high. Rejected: declared and detected values remain in separate fields with the detector confidence retained, and precedence is resolved at read time by a recorded rule.
